author: The Buddha
text: Hatred is never appeased by hatred in this world. By non-hatred alone is hatred appeased. This is a law eternal.

author: The Buddha
text: All that we are is the result of what we have thought.

author: The Buddha
text: Better than a thousand hollow words is one word that brings peace.

author: The Buddha
text: Though one may conquer a thousand times a thousand men in battle, yet he indeed is the noblest victor who conquers himself.

author: The Buddha
text: Just as a solid rock is not shaken by the storm, even so the wise are not affected by praise or blame.

author: The Buddha
text: Overcome the angry by non-anger; overcome the wicked by goodness; overcome the miser by generosity; overcome the liar by truth.

author: The Buddha
text: Just as a mother would protect her only child with her life, even so let one cultivate a boundless love towards all beings.

author: The Buddha
text: Radiating kindness over the entire world.

author: Rumi
text: The wound is the place where the Light enters you.

author: Rumi
text: Lovers don't finally meet somewhere. They're in each other all along.

author: Rumi
text: Out beyond ideas of wrongdoing and rightdoing, there is a field. I'll meet you there.

author: Rumi
text: Let yourself be silently drawn by the strange pull of what you really love. It will not lead you astray.

author: Lao Tzu
text: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.

author: Lao Tzu
text: He who knows others is wise; he who knows himself is enlightened.

author: Lao Tzu
source: Tao Te Ching 15, trans. Stephen Mitchell
text: Do you have the patience to wait till your mud settles and the water is clear?

author: Marcus Aurelius
text: Such as are your habitual thoughts, such also will be the character of your mind; for the soul is dyed by the thoughts.

author: Marcus Aurelius
text: Very little is needed to make a happy life; it is all within yourself, in your way of thinking.

author: Marcus Aurelius
text: Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.

author: Marcus Aurelius
text: Accept the things to which fate binds you, and love the people with whom fate brings you together, but do so with all your heart.

author: Seneca
text: Wherever there is a human being, there is an opportunity for a kindness.

author: Seneca
text: If you wish to be loved, love.

author: Seneca
text: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.

author: Epictetus
text: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the opinions about things.

author: Epictetus
text: No man is free who is not master of himself.

author: Thich Nhat Hanh
text: Breathing in, I calm body and mind. Breathing out, I smile.

author: Thich Nhat Hanh
text: Walk as if you are kissing the Earth with your feet.

author: Kahlil Gibran
text: Love gives naught but itself and takes naught but from itself.

author: Kahlil Gibran
text: Love possesses not nor would it be possessed; for love is sufficient unto love.

author: Kahlil Gibran
text: Your pain is the breaking of the shell that encloses your understanding.

author: Kahlil Gibran
text: Let there be spaces in your togetherness, and let the winds of the heavens dance between you.

author: Kahlil Gibran
text: Work is love made visible.

author: Alan Watts
text: The only way to make sense out of change is to plunge into it, move with it, and join the dance.

author: Ram Dass
text: We're all just walking each other home.

author: Socrates
text: The unexamined life is not worth living.

author: Plato
text: At the touch of love everyone becomes a poet.

author: Aristotle
text: Love is composed of a single soul inhabiting two bodies.

author: Hafiz
text: Even after all this time the sun never says to the earth, "You owe me." Look what happens with a love like that. It lights the whole sky.

author: Rabindranath Tagore
text: Let your life lightly dance on the edges of Time like dew on the tip of a leaf.

author: Rabindranath Tagore
text: The butterfly counts not months but moments, and has time enough.

author: Rainer Maria Rilke
text: Love consists in this, that two solitudes protect and touch and greet each other.

author: Shunryu Suzuki
text: In the beginner's mind there are many possibilities, but in the expert's there are few.

author: Pema Chödrön
text: You are the sky. Everything else is just the weather.
